To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellular pH, total glutathione, and percent oxidized GSH were increased in rabbit corneas following 7 days storage in a moist chamber at 4 C, but were maintained at levels similar to the control corneas in corneas stored in a MK medium.
storage of corneas in MK medium is better than storage of the whole eye in moist chamber for maintaining the intracellular pH and glutthione content of the corneal endothelial cells.
the intracellular pH and glutahione levels in the rabbit cornealendothelium were unchanged following storage for up to 7days, but were altered after 14 days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of storage in a moist chamber and MK storage medium on the corneal endothelial cells of the rabbit.
the effects of prolonged storage of corneas on the intracellular pH and glutamine content of corneal endothelial cells.
the effect of storage on the intracellular pH and glutamine content of corneal endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
storage of the whole eye in moist chamber for 7 days resulted in an increased intracellular total glutamine content and a decreased glutathione oxidation ratio.
, for a 7-day period, MK medium provides a much more stable storage medium than does the aqueous humor.

the pH and glutathine content of the endothelial cells were not significantly affected by 7 days of storage in MK medium, whereas both pH and glutathionine content were affected by 7-day storage of the whole eye.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pH of the corneal endothelial cell remains stable for 7 days following storage in either MK medium or in the aqueous humor of a stored eye.
, although the endothelium was viable for up to 2 weeks, the intracellular pH rose and glutathione oxidation state decreased during the storage period.

the pH and the glutathione levels of corneal endothelia were maintained at near normal levels in corneas stored in the MK medium, while the glutathione level of the endothelia of corneas stored in a moist chamber rose significantly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
storage of rabbit corneal tissue in MK medium with a HEPES buffer for 7 days does not cause significant changes in intracellular pH or glutathione content.
endothelial cells are able to maintain intracellular pH during storage, even when the pH of their surrounding medium has changed significantly.
the isolated cornea stored in MK medium is a better model for studying the effects of storage than is the whole eye stored in a moist chamber.
